answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 43% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and hence nobody profits from it. Because the ledge forfeiture is applied at exit, the knoll ledger totals each burn, and the sonnet audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 196 aliases hence destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
